objectives: Group taught y-initial CVC words by their rime.
Recognize shared endings in yam/ham, yap/map, and yet/pet.
Read short controlled word lists with accurate initial sounds and short vowels.
Explain how changing one phoneme can create a different word.
concepts: A rime includes the vowel and any sounds that follow it.
Words may share a rime while their initial consonants differ.
Changing the initial sound can create a new word in the same family.
Accurate decoding requires attention to both onset and rime.

definitions.definition: The consonant sound or sounds before the vowel in a syllable.
The vowel and the sounds that follow it in a syllable.
A group of words that share a spelling and sound pattern.

workedExamples.solution: Both share the rime -am; their initial sounds are /y/ and /h/.
Both share -ap; the onset changes from /y/ to /m/.
Both share -et; the onset changes from /y/ to /p/.

commonMistakes: Grouping words only because they start with y.
Ignoring the vowel when sorting by rime.
Assuming yak and yam share a rime because both start with y.
Reading a word family by guessing instead of blending.
keyTakeaways: Listen for the vowel and ending together.
Keep onset and rime separate during analysis.
Read each new word after sorting.
Check that the whole word matches its graphemes.

activities.name: Onset-and-rime cards
steps: Place each word card face up.
Underline the vowel and final sound(s).
Group words with the same rime.
Read each group aloud and explain the shared pattern.

activities.name: Change-one-sound ladder
steps: Change the onset to /y/ to make yap.
Keep -ap fixed while reading both words.
Explain which sound changed and which stayed the same.

outcomes: Sort at least 8 of 10 words by their rime accurately.
Distinguish a shared onset from a shared rime.
Decode each word after sorting rather than relying on its group.

options: Sort by vowel-plus-ending rime, not only onset

answerKeys.explanation: Yam and ham share the vowel and final /m/.
Yap and map both end in -ap.
Pet begins /p/ and yet begins /y/; both share -et.
The onset is the initial consonant /y/.
The rime includes the vowel /a/ and final /p/.
The learner must blend the full word, not just guess from the rime.
Yak and yam have different rimes despite sharing the onset.
